item.description: He cut his teeth playing rock stars and pretty posh boys. Speaking from his LA home, the actor talks about landing his first blockbuster lead in the grisly DC horror. Will it be too shocking for comic book fans? Exactly 13 years ago this month, Tom Rhys Harries was hanging by his ankles from a meat hook every night. Playing a teenage rock’n’roll idol abducted by gangsters in a revival of Jez Butterworth’s Mojo, Harries was fresh out of drama school and the only unknown in a cast led by Ben Whishaw and Rupert Grint. item.title: Musical trailblazer Lakecia Benjamin: From chasing Prince to touring with Stevie Wonder
item.description: In this interview with FRANCE 24's Culture editor Eve Jackson, saxophonist Lakecia Benjamin looks back at her distinguished career. From trying to sneak into Prince's Las Vegas shows to catching the attention of Stevie Wonder, the six-time Grammy-nominated musician has carved out a career working with some of the biggest names in music, from Missy Elliott and Jay-Z to Alicia Keys. In 2023, her album "Phoenix", recorded after a near-fatal car accident, earned three Grammy nominations and marked a turning point in her career. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Devil in the detail: 100 years on, FW Murnau’s Faust scrapbook reveals the secrets of his silent masterpiece
item.description: A rediscovered collection of drawings and on-set photos finally reveals the intricate on-set mysteries of one of early cinema’s most gifted pioneers FW Murnau was one of the greatest of all silent film-makers, with a rare genius for making beautiful images on screen. His peers liked to say he “had a camera instead of a head”. The director of such stunning films as vampire tale Nosferatu (1922) and marital romance Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans (1927) died at the age of 42 in 1931, meaning that his career barely scraped into the talkie era. Still, Murnau’s tremendous run of silent pictures… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: 36 mil reproducciones · 334 reacciones | Volta aos palcos - Simaria voltou aos palcos após quatro anos. A cantora gravou um novo DVD, com 13 músicas inéditas, e anunciou a turnê Tô Bem. Em entrevista ao Fantástico neste domingo (11), ela contou por que decidiu se afastar da carreira. “Eu precisava cuidar de mim, da minha saúde mental, do meu corpo, olhar para mim um pouco e olhar para os meus filhos”, disse. A artista também falou sobre o fim da dupla com Simone, anunciado em 2022. Ela revelou que enfrentava um período difícil emocionalmente. Apesar da separação profissional, as irmãs continuam próximas. “Hoje, nós temos uma relação melhor do que quando a gente cantava juntas”, afirmou. Segundo Simaria, as duas trocam conselhos e opiniões sobre as músicas que estão produzindo. Simaria se emocionou ao lembrar dos anos dedicados aos filhos. “Eu pararia mil vezes, mil vezes, se fosse para ficar perto deles, porque eu pude viver os melhores momentos da minha vida”, declarou. A cantora também destacou o apoio da família. “Eles me salvaram, assim, primeiro Deus e depois minha família.” Saiba mais no #g1 #simaria #simoneesimaria #musica | g1 - O Portal de Notícias da globo
